questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good university with relevant courses, as well as a fun and interesting city and country to explore with plenty of things to do. I also wanted to study in an English-speaking country to improve my English.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You had to find most of the information yourself, but everything you needed was available on either the university's website or the UCEAP website. However, I felt that I needed a bit more guidance during the first week. I started on the 5th and attended an information meeting that evening, after classes had already begun, so I was a little confused at first.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much besides the introductory meeting for all international students on the first day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was fairly easy to find accommodation, but rent in Los Angeles is very expensive, so it was difficult to find something within my budget.

I would recommend finding roommates, as it's great to have people around you when you're an international student, and it's also a good way to make friends. I was there with my boyfriend, so I didn't have roommates, but I definitely would have if he hadn't been there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: To get the full college experience, I would recommend living either on campus or very close to it. I lived quite far from campus, but the public transportation was free and easy to use, although it took a long time, but it worked out well. Living farther away also gave me the opportunity to explore more of Los Angeles instead of spending all my time on campus. So, it really depends on what kind of experience you're looking for.

questions.answer: A lot of forms to fill out and information videos to watch

questions.answer: Not sure.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all the classes I wanted, but I had to adjust my course selection several times because some classes were cancelled or had scheduling conflicts.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enroll as soon as registration opens, as classes fill up quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found my classes very interesting, and my professors were great.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a little easier for me to get high grades, but the courses were also bachelor's-level classes. They were still academically challenging, very enjoyable, and I learned a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was much more continuous assessment, with regular homework assignments, essays, a midterm, and a final exam. The exams focused more on remembering and understanding what we had covered in class rather than building on the material or developing new arguments. Many of the exams consisted of multiple-choice questions, short-answer questions, and handwritten essays completed during class. Overall, I found the exams easier than those in Denmark. UCLA also follows a quarter system, so coming from a semester system, everything felt very fast-paced. It seemed like there were always exams or assignments just around the corner.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Health 160: Housing and Homelessness, SOCIOL 140: Negotiating Medical Care: Physician-Patient Conversations, Communication Studies 110
Gender & Communication,  Sociology 122: Sociology of Violence, ANTHRO 136M: MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY, SOC GEN 125: Critical Study of Health, Sickness, & Healing in Global Perspective, Med 88S: The Science, Stigma, and Policy of Women’s Health

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved all my courses, but especially Global Health 160: Housing and Homelessness, as learning about homelessness in Los Angeles, where it is such a major issue, was incredibly interesting. I also really enjoyed SOC GEN 125: Critical Study of Health, Sickness, & Healing in Global Perspective, COMM 188: Cultural Diversity and Mass Communication, and Gender Studies 10: Introduction to Gender Studies.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had a different health insurance plan than the one offered by the university, so I had to pay for some doctor visits myself. This was an unexpected expense, but the consultations were not as expensive as I had expected ($25 per visit).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are more expensive than in Denmark, and rent is also very high.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use them much myself, but there are plenty of clubs and activities to get involved in if you want to.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a club for almost everything—hiking, sports, surfing, and much more. You can also use the gym for free and sign up for fitness classes such as yoga, Pilates, and Zumba for an additional fee.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend joining a club, such as the Backpacking Club, which organizes weekend hikes and camping trips, or the Surf Club, where you can learn to surf.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the beaches (Malibu, Venice, Santa Monica, and Laguna), go hiking in the beautiful nature around Los Angeles, and explore neighborhoods such as Downtown LA, Silver Lake, Los Feliz, and Hollywood. If you have the time—and ideally access to a car—I also highly recommend visiting nearby national parks like Joshua Tree, Sequoia, and Yosemite, as well as the Big Sur coastline.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: At first, I was a little surprised that people didn't socialize much in the classroom, and I wasn't sure how to make friends. My advice is to join clubs and simply start talking to people in your classes—everyone is very friendly and open. I also attended the introduction meeting and events for international students, which were a great way to meet new people since everyone there is looking to make friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A much heavier workload, with more homework and assignments throughout the term.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and welcoming attitude of the people. I was invited to events after just one conversation, which would probably never happen in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be brave and reach out to people, join clubs, go on trips, and explore places outside campus, such as LA and the national parks. Be thorough when researching the courses you want to take, and make sure to enroll quickly when registration opens!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for pre-approval at KU well in advance, and make sure to carefully read and understand all the information you receive.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned so much and found my classes really interesting and rewarding! I also became much more independent and learned to step outside my comfort zone. One of the best parts was getting to explore so much of California—we went on weekend trips throughout the semester and did a road trip afterwards, which was such an amazing experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maybe seeing so many people experiencing homelessness. It really affected me, and in general, I often felt frustrated with the political situation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
